comments.author: @jonholzworth4463
comments.text:
The amount of misinformation in this video is astounding. And the premise is false. The notion that American houses need to be replaced every 50 years is laughable. They make it seem like most houses in the US are built with slab-on-grade foundations. Perhaps most houses being built today are built that way, but they are still a minority of the houses. Any house in a cold-weather state will have a footer that is below the frost line. Where I live that is a minimum of 3 feet underground. I've been to 32 states in this country and I've never been inside a slab-on-grade house. 

Then there is the fallacy of the brick walls being better. For one, houses in the UK aren't built with bricks. They are built with concrete block. The fact that the video got such a simple thing wrong is a great indicator of the knowledge behind the rest of the video. The exterior walls of your home serve two purposes. The first is to hold the roof up. The second is to prevent anything outside the home from coming into the home. The wood framed walls in the US accomplish this goal just fine. And as I said earlier, we don't have a problem with our wooden walls deteriorating quickly. So, the "far superior" block walls of UK homes don't actually serve a purpose. This is especially true when you consider that homes in the US withstand hurricanes, tornadoes, earthquakes, blizzards, and more. Why exactly would we need walls made of concrete block?

I guess if we had roofs covered in concrete we might need block walls to keep the roof from collapsing the entire house. But since we don't sheath our roofs in concrete we don't have that issue. Which brings me to another point. Having to replace your roof every 3 decades, at most is not some major inconvenience. And he vastly overstated how often our roofs need to be replaced. The roof on my house is probably 40 years old. His cost estimate was only the materials cost. A new roof will be installed on your home in two days. And there is a lot of competition so the actual installation cost is significantly lower than the cost of a British concrete shingled roof. Even repairing concrete shingles becomes more expensive than replacing an entire roof of asphalt shingles very quickly. One last thing about American roofs. Asphalt isn't exactly a flimsy material. It's not like we are covering our roofs with paper.

Interior walls made of concrete aren't just overkill, they are much worse than wood framing. They get in the way of all sorts of things, least of which is duct work. Think about it, you'd need a freaking hammer drill just to hang some shelves on the wall. No thanks. They claim that we only use central heating and air because it's cheaper and only made possible by our wood framing. Yes, the initial cost of installing duct work is more expensive than plumbing a hot water heating system. But, that cost is more than offset by the significantly cheaper build cost of wood framed interior walls. And if radiators were the superior method of heating a home, that's what US homes would be using. It's not like we can't install radiators in a wood frame home. I have radiators in my 109 year old wood framed home, and I wish i had central heating. That's also a big reason why air conditioners aren't popular in the UK. It's not because they don't need them. The cost is easily justifiable when you consider the life of an AC unit. If British homes could install affordable, effective AC units that didn't look like a large appliance hanging on a wall in every room, they'd have a lot more air conditioned homes. 

And, then we get to the most absurd and insulting claim of the whole video. The claim that houses in the UK somehow require more skilled labor than in the US which leads to a lower quality of build. That's some of the dumbest shit I've ever heard. Do the people who made this video think masons need a fucking master's degree or something. If I had to rank the intelligence of the craftsmen in each trade, masons would be near the bottom, just barely edging out drywall finishers and roofers. I say that as someone who was a mason for over ten years. Carpenters have to do a lot more math than masons. Masons have to learn one skill and learn how to do it as quickly as possible. Only one guy in each crew needs to be able to read and do basic math. The most mentally taxing part of being a mason is reading your brick rule. Like my boss used to always say when I was an apprentice, "this job takes a strong back and a weak mind." The person who researched this video has at least half of the qualities necessary to be a mason. I don't know how strong his back is though.
